svg.title: Figure 1. The path of one write
svg.desc: Five tiers from top to bottom. The writer, one process with no network call for any check, holds the schema map and derives the family and the subject (72 ns), matches the grant (66 ns), finds the stream (87 ns) and validates the record (15.2 µs for 726 bytes). At a site, the write goes to a NATS leaf server on loopback whose one-replica stream acknowledges it, and the hub's stream sources it when the line returns; with no site, the writer publishes to the hub. The hub, a three-node JetStream cluster, repeats the grant match and stream lookup; a schema id the map lacks has the family unknown, which no stream binds, so the write fails closed. The projector, one durable consumer per stream, checks the address, validates again, parks records whose schema has not arrived, and applies the position guard and node tombstones (Lemmas 1 and 2). The Postgres read model has seven tables, each with one forced row policy, and a read binds its role and tenant in the same round trip.
